h1: What work is restricted within the 100-foot wetland buffer zone in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Wetland Buffer Zone Rules: Work Near Wetlands and Streams
description: Find out why grading, construction, drainage, and vegetation work near wetlands may require Conservation Commission review.
short_answer: Newton requires Conservation Commission review for land-altering work within 100 feet of a vegetated wetland, intermittent stream, or pond. The City also identifies a 200-foot review area near perennial streams. The exact restrictions depend on the resource area, proposed activity, and applicable exemptions.

facts.text: Newton identifies the 100-foot area near vegetated wetlands, intermittent streams, and ponds as an area where land-altering work must be reviewed and permitted by the Conservation Commission.
Newton lists grading, construction, tree or shrub removal, and drainage projects among land-altering activities subject to review.

qa.q: Can I grade or install drainage within the 100-foot area without checking?
qa.a: No. Newton expressly lists grading and drainage projects among activities that may require Conservation Commission review.
